chunks: To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth. Verily He is all-sufficient, worthy of praise.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is Al-Ghani and Al-Hamid in Surah Luqman?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the ontological independence of Allah (Al-Ghani) contrasted with the absolute dependence of creation, a concept central to the doctrine of Tawhid. It serves as a foundational reminder that all praise (Al-Hamid) is due to Him alone, reinforcing the believer's reliance on the Divine Source of all sufficiency.
